claim: The official tourist office route through Menton old town links Saint-Michel Archangel Basilica (1639), the Pénitents Blancs Chapel (1680-1687) and the Vieux Château cemetery, with notable burials of architect Hans-Georg Tersling and rugby inventor William Webb Ellis.
quote: Saint-Michel Archangel Basilica (built 1639): A Baroque masterpiece with a 53m bell tower... Vieux Château Cemetery: Overlooks the bay with notable burials including architect Hans-Georg Tersling and rugby inventor William Webb Ellis

claim: The Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange was built between 1640 and 1653 on the foundations of two earlier 14th-15th century churches dedicated to Saint Michel, and is a minor basilica still serving as the Catholic parish church of Menton's historic core.
quote: The Basilica of Saint-Michel-Archange of Menton is a minor basilica and a Catholic parish church located in the heart of the historic center of Menton. It was erected between 1640 and 1653 on the vestiges of two churches from the 14th and 15th centuries

claim: The Parvis Saint-Michel's calade was rebuilt in 2006 with 250,000 pebbles selected one by one from the Careï and Borrigo beaches, laid across 170 m² to form the Grimaldi arms and an H for Prince Honoré of Monaco.
quote: The Parvis was completely renovated in 2006, requiring 250,000 pebbles to reconstitute the 170 m². These small stones were selected one by one for their color and shape from the beaches of Careï and Borrigo... arms of the Grimaldi family as well as a letter H for 'Prince Honoré'

claim: The Rampes Saint-Michel were commissioned by Prince Honoré III in 1753 to link the seafront to the Basilique Saint-Michel; the upper section is a listed historical monument and the lower stretch dates from a Second World War restoration.
quote: The Escaliers, also known as Les Rampes Saint-Michel, were built on the orders of Prince Honoré III, who ordered them built in 1753. The upper part of the ramps is listed as a historical monument and dates from the middle of the 18th century, while the lower part dates from the Second World War

claim: The Basilique Saint-Michel is open Monday-Friday 15:00-17:00 and Saturday 10:00-12:00 and 15:00-17:00, closed Sunday except for the 11:00 Sunday mass, with free entry.
quote: The basilica is open Monday through Friday between 3 pm and 5 pm, on Saturday between 10 am and 12 pm and between 3 pm and 5 pm, and is closed on Sunday. However, it is accessible on Sundays at 11:00 am for mass

claim: The Chapelle des Pénitents Blancs (also called Chapelle de l'Immaculée Conception), built from 1680 and consecrated in 1687 on land donated by Prince Louis I Grimaldi, is a Baroque Catholic Reformation chapel listed as a Monument Historique in 1947 and sits adjacent to the Basilique.
quote: The chapel of the Immaculate Conception, or White Penitents, was built from 1680, in the Capitol district, on land outside the walls of the medieval city, donated by Prince Louis I Grimaldi... It was declared a Historical Monument in 1947

claim: The Cimetière du Vieux-Château is open 07:00-19:00 from April to October (08:00-17:00 in winter), free, sits 5 minutes from the Basilique at the start of Boulevard du Garavan, and contains a golden-domed Russian Orthodox chapel reflecting Menton's 19th-century convalescent community.
quote: Hours: 7 a.m.–7 p.m. (April–October); 8 a.m.–5 p.m. (November–March)... approximately a 5-minute walk from the Basilique Saint-Michel... A Russian Orthodox chapel with a golden dome reflects the 19th-century Russian community

claim: Lonely Planet recommends meandering up through the old town to the hilltop Cimetière du Vieux-Château for sweeping views over the old town and port — built on the site of Menton's demolished medieval château.
quote: For great views of the old town and the port, meander all the way up through the historic quarter to this hilltop cemetery

claim: Quai Bonaparte was inaugurated on 14 August after a €4.5 million refit between the Bastion and Victoria roundabouts, adding tiled paving, a sea-side cycle path, LED lighting and plantings of centenarian olive trees, palms and citrus along the old-town waterfront.
quote: the requalification of Quai Bonaparte on August 14th, situated between the Bastion roundabout and the Victoria traffic circle. The €4.5 million project featured quality finishes including tiled paving on the built-up side... centennial olive trees, palms, citrus

claim: Rue Longue is the main artery of Menton's old town, running parallel to Quai Bonaparte between the Saint-Julien gate (east) and Saint-Antoine gate (southwest) on the line of the ancient Roman Via Julia Augusta.
quote: Rue Longue, parallel to the Quai Bonaparte, is the main artery of the old town, running between the Saint-Julien gate in the East and the Saint-Antoine gate in the Southwest, following the route of the ancient Roman road Julia Augusta

claim: The signature postcard view of Menton — pastel houses stacked beneath the Basilique with the Rampes Saint-Michel as focal point — is captured from the jetty at the end of Quai Napoléon III / Quai Impératrice Eugénie, best in morning light.
quote: The most famous view in Menton is found at the end of Quai Impératrice Eugénie, where Menton's colorful houses rise against the hillside, with the Basilique Saint-Michel Archange and the Rampe Saint-Michel creating the perfect focal points
